apis.name: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) — seller accounts
apis.authentication: Login with Amazon (OAuth 2.0). Private applications are self-authorised by the Primary User of the seller account and receive a refresh token; public applications are authorised by each selling partner through OAuth and must be re-authorised annually.
apis.eligibility: Seller with a Professional selling account registering as a private developer (application only for its own organisation; max 10 self-authorisations; no OAuth by other companies), or a public developer authorised by other sellers (25 seller authorisations if not listed in the Selling Partner Appstore, unlimited if listed). Developer Profile with roles, use cases and security controls is reviewed by Amazon. A brand that is not a seller or vendor has no account to authorise.

own_listings: title, bullets, description, attributes and images as submitted (Listings Items API)
catalogue view: item name, brand, attributes, identifiers, images, classifications, variations (Catalog Items API)
A+ content published by the account (A+ Content API)
price and offer (Listings Items API offers)
featured offer / Buy Box data, featured offer expected price, competitive price threshold (Product Pricing API, sellers only)
stock availability (Listings Items fulfillmentAvailability)
listing issues with severity, categories and enforcement actions incl. search suppression
Suppressed Listings report
attribute requirements per product type (Product Type Definitions API)
sales rank (Catalog Items salesRanks)
sales and traffic: page views, sessions, Buy Box percentage, conversion (Sales and Traffic report, Data Kiosk)
search data: Search Query Performance, Search Catalog Performance, Market Basket, Repeat Purchase, Search Terms (Brand Analytics; Brand Registry required)
review counts: totalReviewCount, lowRatingReviewCount, criticalReviewRate (Data Kiosk Seller Analytics)
review topics, mentions, star-rating impact and up to three snippets per topic (Customer Feedback API; US, UK, FR, IT, DE, ES, JP only)
push notifications: listing status, listing issues, branded item content change, offer changes, pricing health, hourly traffic
competitor_listings: catalogue facts for any ASIN: item name, brand, attributes, images, identifiers, classifications, variations (Catalog Items API)
sales rank for any ASIN (Catalog Items API)
lowest-priced and featured offers for any ASIN: seller id, price, shipping, Buy Box winner, number of offers (Product Pricing API, seller accounts only)
most-clicked ASINs per search term with click share and conversion share (Amazon Search Terms report; Brand Registry, brand representative)
category-level review and return topics (Customer Feedback API browse-node operations)
NOT available: star rating, review count, review text, Q&A, stock, A+ content of other sellers

official_quality_score.note: The SP-API documentation index lists no listing-quality or content score. Closest official signals: listing issues with enforcement actions, the Suppressed Listings report and Product Type Definitions requirement schemas.

apis.limitations: No content or price history (snapshots must be stored). Brand Analytics reports need Brand Registry; Search Query Performance, Search Catalog Performance and Market Basket are not listed for South Africa. Customer Feedback API not offered for AE, SA, IN or ZA. Product Pricing API is for sellers only. ANY_OFFER_CHANGED notifications only for items with an active offer. Amazon states that not every listing problem has a defined issue. Use is limited by the Solution Provider Portal Agreement, Acceptable Use Policy and Data Protection Policy. UNVERIFIED: whether Customer Feedback returns data for ASINs the account does not sell; whether every Data Kiosk metric is served for South Africa.
apis.rate_limits: Token bucket per account-application pair. Defaults (requests per second / burst): getCatalogItem 2/2; searchCatalogItems 2/2; getListingsItem 5/5 (reference page shows burst 10); Product Type Definitions 5/5; getCompetitiveSummary 0.033/1; getFeaturedOfferExpectedPriceBatch 0.033/1; getItemOffers 0.5/1; getItemOffersBatch 0.1/1; createReport 0.0167/15; getReport 2/15; Data Kiosk createQuery 0.0167/15; Customer Feedback operations 1/10; A+ getContentDocument 10-20 (documentation pages differ).
apis.pricing: No API fee in force. The third-party developer fee programme announced in November 2025 (USD 1,400 per year plus GET-call usage tiers) was cancelled; Amazon states it will not move forward with the fees 'at this time'. Secondary reports say sellers and vendors using the API only for their own business were never in scope. A Professional selling account is required for a private seller application (plan price UNVERIFIED).
apis.historical_data: Data Kiosk seller analytics: start date no more than two years back. Search Query Performance: maximum monthly reporting period 17 months. Customer Feedback trends: six months. Listing content, issues and prices: current state only.
apis.competitor_monitoring_note: Catalogue and offer data for other sellers' ASINs is technically returned, and Amazon documents repricers that watch competitor prices as an intended use. The agreement provides data 'solely for the purpose of supporting an Authorized User's business with Amazon'; the Acceptable Use Policy forbids retrieving information not necessary for the application, aggregating data across authorised users, and using external data services that vend data retrieved from Amazon's websites. Interpretation requires legal review.
apis.integration_complexity_note: Developer registration with security questionnaire and role approval, per-operation rate limits, asynchronous reports and an audited data-protection policy.

apis.historical_data: Listing Quality report accepts a snapshot date up to the previous two years; item details include historical quality score trends.
apis.competitor_monitoring_note: Catalogue search is documented for deciding the item set-up path, not for monitoring; terms of use not reviewed.
apis.integration_complexity_note: Simple key-based access for own account; many report types; tight limits on quality endpoints.
